newsitem.title: USA: Georgia MEAG says plans $200 mln refunding.
newsitem.headline: Georgia MEAG says plans $200 mln refunding.

text.p: Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia plans a $200 million refunding of its senior lien bonds this week or next week, depending on market conditions Ronald Vazquez, vice president of financial services said Wednesday.
"We were very close yesterday," Vazquez said.
JP Morgan Securities is senior manager for the negotiated deal, he said.
The authority, known as MEAG, has also signed an agreement with the Municipal Gas Authority of Georgia to form an allianceto jointly market services to Georgia municipalities.
The alliance will focus initially on analysis and performance-based contracting, but may later act in a brokering capacity aggregating gas and electric loads of the cities, the company said.
